newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends down 78 cents on weak gas oil, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends down 78 cents on weak gas oil, NYMEX.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended 78 cents lower after breaching $22 a barrel for the first time in four months on Thurday on fund selling encourged by drastically weaker gas oil and NYMEX futures, traders said.
March IPE Brent crude futures settled at $21.69 a barrel.
"There was excellent trade selling the whole way down ... It's a break (below $22) whichever way you look at it. It's fallen out of bed," a trader said.
The next support level on the continuation chart is $21.45, then $21.00, traders said.
Prompt Brent futures had not fallen below $22 since September 23, 1996, when it touched a low of $21.83, although the front-month touched $22 on December 11 and January 27.
The psychological impact of the breach of $22, combined with a steep decline in NYMEX crude and heating oil, propelled the contract dowards to a range between $21.60 and $21.70 in the late afternoon.
February IPE gas oil futures slid $9.25 to settle at $191.75 a tonne, after dipping below key resistance at $195.50 on technical factors and plays on the Feb/March gas oil spread.

Traders said that despite a squeeze on Feburary gas oil the contract has come under pressure from the large amount of material accumulated in the Rotterdam region and the closure of the arb to the United States.
